newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia posts flat profit, future savings.
newsitem.headline: Skandia posts flat profit, future savings.

text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia Insurance Co Ltd said on Wednesday a restructuring programme cost the company 1.4 billion crowns ($183.5 million) in 1996 but was expected to give long-term savings of 400 million crowns annually.

Posting a flat operating profit for 1996, Skandia said in its results statement measures adopted during the year to raise productivity and enhance long-term earnings capacity entailed a 2.2 billion crown charge against earnings.

But the company proposed a higher dividend of 2.75 crowns per share against two crowns last year and said it had adopted a new dividend policy corresponding to 15 to 25 percent of operating profit after tax.
"1996 was a good year for Skandia with improved profitability in both the non-life insurance operations and the savings operations," said Skandia's chief executive Lars-Eric Petersson in a statement.
Skandia posted a one percent rise in operating profit to 2.39 billion crowns and a 12 percent return on net asset value after taxes compared to 14 percent in 1995.
Its pre-tax profit for 1996 was 1.65 billion crowns against market expectations of a pre-tax profit of 3.06 billion crowns.
Skandia's shares slipped to 220 crowns on the report but quickly recovered ground and were trading at 225.5 crowns, 2.5 crowns lower than Tuesday's close, in afternoon trade.
The group's operating result for non-life insurance and reinsurance operations rose 54 percent to 3.52 billion crowns.
Its life and unit linked assurance operations showed continued growth, with operating result rising 41 percent to 1.52 billion crowns and premiums written up 45 percent.

The group's total premiums written climbed 16 percent to 58.79 billion crowns of which 22.46 billion crowns came from non-life insurance and reinsurance and 36.42 billion crowns from life and unit linked assurance.
One broker said the market was a bit disappointed that Skandia did not announce a spin off of its unit linked assurance operations, Assurance & Financial Services (AFS).

Skandia said it was pursuing its strategy while being careful to level the risk in a balanced non-life insurance and reinsurance portfolio, have a stronger focus on life assurance and savings products and a strong financial position.
"Over the longterm the group's returns on investment should correspond to the ten-year Swedish government bond rate plus five percentage points," the company said.
"Based on the current level of interest rates the return on investment over time should be a miniumum of 12 percent after taxes."
Skandia said its longterm strategy had required streamlining and a focus on core business.
Restructing costs of 1.4 billion crowns were charged against 1996 earnings.

About 100 people left the Nordic operations in 1996 due to rationalisation and a further 300 would be cut over the next three years during an action plan to increase competitiveness in Nordic operations.
"The action programme, the restructing and the investments in new technology are expected to lead to annual savings of 400 million crowns in three years' time," Skandia said.
The company said its new dividend policy took into account the growth potential of the group's core businesses.

"It is the board's ambition that the dividend should correspond to the group's long-term result development and amount to between 15-25 percent of the operating profit after full tax and minority interests," it said.
($ = 7.628 Swedish Crowns)
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
